spark.scene: True-color view of the Hawaiian Islands from northwest to southeast over dark ocean with scattered to extensive bright white cumulus and cirrus. Largest island in southeast partly cloudy with northern cloud cap and visible brown-green land; faint grayish streak extends southward from the island over the ocean.

plumes.label: thin gray streak south of the large island
plumes.visual_description: narrow translucent gray filament extending southward from the southeastern island over dark ocean, distinct from brighter white cumulus and cirrus nearby

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

evidence: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea WATCH/ORANGE and erupting yes with glowing vents emitting flames/spatter, Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN and not erupting, favoring Kilauea vog over Mauna Loa. [E2]
FIRMS on 2026-09-18 shows no fire clusters in box around Hawaii Island but 51 volcanic-thermal pixels at Kilauea summit, supporting volcanic not wildfire-smoke source. [E6]
3-hr GOES-West tracking gives source end at 19.43,-155.2 only 9.1 km from Kilauea summit vs 43.1 km from Mauna Loa summit, indicating plume trails from Kilauea. [E4]

Motion vs wind disagreement: wind from 70 deg (toward 250 deg) vs measured drift toward 192 deg = ~58 deg difference, outside ~45 deg agreement; fit R2 0.47 is modest and drift speed 6.2 km/h is much slower than 44.4 km/h wind but expected to be slower for source-attached plume, so direction mismatch lowers confidence. [E1, E4]

Narrow translucent gray filament extending southward over dark ocean distinct from bright white cumulus/cirrus; mask 155 km long, 5223 km2, only 14.1% land over Hawaii Island with no island swallowed, so mask is reliable and not a cloud bank. [E5, E3]

evidence_cited.text: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea WATCH/ORANGE and erupting yes with glowing vents emitting flames/spatter, Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN and not erupting, favoring Kilauea vog over Mauna Loa.
FIRMS on 2026-09-18 shows no fire clusters in box around Hawaii Island but 51 volcanic-thermal pixels at Kilauea summit, supporting volcanic not wildfire-smoke source.
3-hr GOES-West tracking gives source end at 19.43,-155.2 only 9.1 km from Kilauea summit vs 43.1 km from Mauna Loa summit, indicating plume trails from Kilauea.

Motion vs wind disagreement: wind from 70 deg (toward 250 deg) vs measured drift toward 192 deg = ~58 deg difference, outside ~45 deg agreement; fit R2 0.47 is modest and drift speed 6.2 km/h is much slower than 44.4 km/h wind but expected to be slower for source-attached plume, so direction mismatch lowers confidence.

Narrow translucent gray filament extending southward over dark ocean distinct from bright white cumulus/cirrus; mask 155 km long, 5223 km2, only 14.1% land over Hawaii Island with no island swallowed, so mask is reliable and not a cloud bank.

classify.caveats: Thin faint streak in mostly cloudy scene; tracked drift toward 192 deg differs ~58 deg from ERA5 wind-implied transport toward ~250 deg (from 70 deg) exceeding 45-deg agreement threshold with low-moderate fit R2 0.47, so transport story is imperfect and confidence reduced despite strong vent proximity.

kilauea.activity_summary: There is currently no active lava on the ground. The north, south, and west vents continue to glow and emit flames, with minor intermittent spatter. Minor summit inflation occurred overnight.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
